advices: Avoid non-essential driving. Driving in heavy snow is extremely dangerous and discouraged for visitors without winter driving experience.
Ensure your rental vehicle is equipped with studless winter tires and carry snow chains.
If visibility drops due to a whiteout, turn on your hazard lights, reduce speed, and pull over to a safe area or a 'Michi no Eki' (roadside rest area).
Look for the downward-pointing red arrow poles (snow poles) on the side of the road to know where the road boundaries are when lines are covered.
If your car gets stuck in the snow, contact emergency services and stay inside the vehicle unless a safe building is clearly visible nearby.
Crucial: Clear the snow around your car's exhaust pipe frequently. A blocked exhaust pipe will cause deadly carbon monoxide to fill the cabin.
Keep the engine off as much as possible while waiting for help. If you must run the heater, ventilate the car by opening windows slightly.
Walk like a penguin with small, shuffling steps, keeping your center of gravity forward to avoid slipping on icy or packed snow surfaces.
Dress in layers. Wear thermal underwear, a windproof and waterproof outer jacket, gloves, and a hat that covers your ears.
Wear winter boots with deep treads. Consider buying attachable snow grips (spikes) for your shoes at local convenience stores.
Keep your hands out of your pockets to maintain balance and protect yourself if you fall. Use a backpack instead of carrying bags in your hands.
Be extremely cautious of snow sliding off roofs or sharp icicles falling from buildings above you, especially on sunny days following a blizzard.
If a severe blizzard or whiteout starts, visibility can drop to zero. Take shelter in the nearest sturdy building, convenience store, or station immediately.
Trains, Shinkansen (bullet trains), flights, and buses are highly likely to experience significant delays or cancellations during Heavy Snow warnings.
Always have a backup plan. Consider staying at an accommodation near the airport the night before a major flight.
Do not wait at unsheltered bus stops or open train platforms for long periods to avoid hypothermia.
Check real-time transit apps, airline websites, and JR English status pages before heading to the station or airport.
If stranded at a station or airport, remain calm, follow the instructions of the staff, and stay in designated heated waiting areas.

When a Heavy Snow or Blizzard Warning is.situation: I am inside a building or accommodation
advices: Stay indoors. Do not go outside to check the weather or take photos during a severe blizzard.
Prepare for possible power outages. Keep your mobile devices fully charged and keep flashlights and warm blankets accessible.
If the power goes out, wear layered clothing indoors to preserve body heat. Do NOT use outdoor charcoal grills or camp stoves indoors for heating, as this causes carbon monoxide poisoning.
Water pipes can freeze and burst in extreme cold. Follow your accommodation's instructions on leaving faucets dripping slightly at night to prevent freezing.
Keep emergency supplies such as drinking water, instant food, and basic first aid items stocked in your room.
If you are staying at a rental house and need to clear snow, never work alone. Always clear snow in pairs or groups and only during the daylight.
Avoid risky tasks such as climbing onto the roof to remove snow unless you have proper safety gear, including a helmet and safety rope.
If using a mechanical snow blower and it gets jammed, ALWAYS turn off the engine completely before attempting to clear the snow from the chute with a stick.
Take frequent breaks while shoveling snow to avoid exhaustion or heart strain.

When a Heavy Snow or Blizzard Warning is.situation: Preparing for a blizzard / Before going out
advices: Download the 'Safety tips' app provided by the Japan Tourism Agency to receive push notifications for Heavy Snow and Blizzard Warnings in multiple languages.
Monitor the Japan Meteorological Agency (JMA) website for color-coded weather warnings and snow depth analysis.
If authorities announce a 'once-in-a-few-years blizzard', cancel your outdoor plans and stay indoors, even if the weather appears calm at the moment.
Ensure you have enough cash on hand, as ATMs and card readers may stop working if power and communication lines are severed.
